limitations.statement: Published total-query statements are not adopted here: initialization is forced; K=0 completion is local; p.22 (24) has an unsupported constant. The separate MSE target supplies a complete local argument.
This is an execution rule for a selected estimator, not an unrestricted Oracle Complexity characterization, a lower bound or an SOSP guarantee.

variants.cost: Forced first call: exactly n stochastic gradient samples, zero HVP samples. Later calls with g_prev!=bottom: conditional expected gradient count b*n and HVP count (1-b)*K, including K=0 on zero segments. Reset branch uses n queries; nonreset uses K. Local vector sums, interpolation and Bernoulli draws are additional arithmetic/randomness, not oracle queries. No full-Hessian storage, same-seed multipoint queries or function-value samples are required.
variants.implementation_details_ref: PDF p.8 Algorithm 1; p.6 oracle; local K=0 completion explicitly identified here.
variants.name: HVP-RVR with forced initial reset and explicit zero-segment branch
variants.output: One vector g approximating grad F(x), generally biased outside reset steps.
public_inputs: Accuracy e>0, reset probability 0<b<=1, variance bounds sigma1>0 and sigma2>=0, Hessian Lipschitz bound L2>=0; require sigma2^2+L2*e>0.
variants.query_and_update: Set n=ceil(5*sigma1^2/e^2), D=x-x_prev, K=ceil(5*(sigma2^2+L2*e)*||D||^2/(b*e^2)). Draw independent C~Bernoulli(b). If C=1 or g_prev=bottom, return (1/n) sum_(j=1)^n G(x,z_j). Otherwise, if D=0, return g_prev without oracle calls (local completion of undefined printed K=0 interpolation). If D!=0, set h=D/K, x^k=x_prev+k*h for k=0,...,K, query independent HVPs H(x^(k-1),z_k)h for k=1,...,K and return g_prev plus their sum.
variants.requirements: F is C^2 with globally L2-Lipschitz Hessian. For every x in R^d: unbiased G(x,z), symmetric unbiased H(x,z), E||G-grad F||^2<=sigma1^2, E||H-Hess F||op^2<=sigma2^2. Every draw is fresh and independent of query history and reset coins; HVP query at (x,v) returns H(x,z)v. Euclidean vector norm and matrix operator norm. The precision/noise domain excludes n=0 and degenerate sigma2=L2=0. MSE guarantees have separate query-sequence restrictions.
variants.state_and_initialization: Per call input x,x_prev in R^d and g_prev in R^d or bottom. Initialize g_0=bottom. The caller stores the returned estimate and previous point for the next call. The first call resets irrespective of the coin.
variants.tuning_and_stopping: n and K are recomputed from the displayed public bounds; one call returns one gradient estimate. There is no optimization stopping rule in this estimator; the caller supplies points and decides when to stop.

issues.note: Zero-displacement return is local; p.8 interpolation otherwise divides by K=0.
